doc.title: Jimmy Witherspoon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, FL, April 12, 1996

title: Monterey Jazz Festival triumph
summary: His mother heard him sing blues live for the first time at Monterey; he was added unbilled and broke it up with Ben Webster and others.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: Accommodations a little better most of the time? And you get to fly I guess. What since the, oh, tell me about the Monterey Jazz Festival, which seems to have been a nice point in your career.
It was the first time she’d ever heard me sing the blues in person.
She is a very religious woman and she wouldn’t go to no, you know, no night clubs. And a delight for me.
So there you are at the Monterey Jazz Festival with some pretty good sidemen.

You know the funny thing about that night, the audience didn’t know I was there. They found me in Newport, Kentucky. So I wasn’t even on the bill. And everybody was leaving, and Jimmy Lyon said, “Hold it, hold it, we’re not through.” And they called me in, and I was with some insignificant musicians by the name of Ben Webster, who else
was there, Bobby Brookmeyer, Roy Eldridge, Woody Herman, Coleman Hawkins, Earl Hines. What can you say?
